concepts.def: Underlying economic, territorial and ideological rivalries, such as the alliance blocs and arms races that preceded the First World War.
Immediate crises and triggers, such as the assassination of Franz Ferdinand in June 1914 or the German invasion of Poland in September 1939.
Twentieth-century wars mobilised whole societies and economies through conscription, rationing, propaganda and the home front.
Technology shaped fighting: trench warfare and artillery dominated the First World War, while blitzkrieg, strategic bombing and atomic weapons marked the Second.
Civilians suffered occupation, bombing of cities, genocide including the Holocaust, and mass displacement of refugees.
Outcomes included peace settlements such as Versailles in 1919, new organisations like the United Nations in 1945, territorial change and social transformation.

walkthroughs.body_html:
World History Topic: Causes & Effects of 20th-Century Wars — a core area of History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

World History Topic: Causes & Effects of 20th-Century Wars brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with World History Topic: Causes & Effects of 20th-Century Wars.

mcqs.q: Which event triggered the outbreak of the First World War?
options: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo in June 1914
The German invasion of Poland
The Russian Revolution
The sinking of the Lusitania
A conflict mobilising a society's entire economy and population, blurring the line between home front and battlefield
A war fought on every continent at once
A war declared by every member of the United Nations
A war fought only with nuclear weapons

mcqs.q: Which of these is a long-term cause of the Second World War?
options: German resentment of the Treaty of Versailles
The attack on Pearl Harbor
The Cuban Missile Crisis
The assassination of Franz Ferdinand

mcqs.q: Which of these was an effect of the Second World War?
options: The founding of the United Nations in 1945
The creation of the League of Nations
The unification of Germany in 1871
The collapse of the Soviet Union

mcqs.q: Did the First World War happen only because Franz Ferdinand was shot?
options: No - the assassination was the spark; underlying alliance systems, militarism, imperial rivalry and the July Crisis decisions turned it into a general war.
Wars have no effects once a peace treaty is signed.
The First World War began over a dispute about colonial trade in Africa alone.
One assassination on its own caused the First World War.

mcqs.q: Did the Treaty of Versailles make the Second World War inevitable?
options: No - it created grievances, but two decades of choices intervened: the Depression, Hitler's decisions, the failure of collective security and appeasement; historians still debate the weighting.
Wars have no effects once a peace treaty is signed.
The Treaty of Versailles was never actually signed.
Versailles alone automatically caused the Second World War.

mcqs.q: Are the effects of war only military and territorial?
options: Wars have no effects once a peace treaty is signed.
No - twentieth-century wars also transformed societies: women's roles, welfare states, decolonisation pressures, refugee movements and new international bodies.
The Treaty of Versailles was never actually signed.
The results of a war are just casualty figures and changed borders.
